title: Updated estimates of neural tube defects prevented by mandatory folic acid fortification - United States, 1995-2011
authors: Williams J, Mai CT, Mulinare J, Isenburg J, Flood TJ, Ethen M, et al.
journal: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
population: Spina bifida and anencephaly among deliveries in 19 US population-based birth defects surveillance programmes, 8 with prenatal ascertainment including stillbirths and terminations
funder: not stated. Authors from the CDC National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities (one also Carter Consulting), the Arizona, Texas and Minnesota health departments and the University of South Florida; published by CDC.
result: In programmes with prenatal ascertainment, anencephaly and spina bifida fell from 10.7 per 10,000 live births in 1995-1996 to 7.0 per 10,000 in 1999-2011, 35% fewer; across all programmes 28% fewer, and 21% in programmes without prenatal ascertainment. Estimated 1326 (95% CI 1122 to 1531) births a year without the defects that would otherwise have been affected. Prevalence remained stable after the initial fall; Hispanic women had the highest prevalence throughout.
